title: SC-300 Domain 1 questions (1.3, 1.4)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Microsoft.

questions.stem: Fabrikam lets partners join as guests. The security team wants guests to be unable to view other users' profiles, groups or group memberships, even for groups the guests belong to. Which guest user access level should you set?
choices: Limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects, the default level
Same access as member users
Limited access, with guests blocked from joining Microsoft 365 groups
Restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects
questions.answer: Restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects
questions.explanation: The most restrictive guest user access level lets guests view only their own profile and objects. The default level (limited access) still lets guests read some details of other users and the groups they belong to, so it does not meet the requirement.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys allows any member user to invite guests. Auditors require that only a small help desk team can invite external users, and those staff must have no other administrative permissions. Which built-in role should you assign to the help desk staff after restricting invitations to admin roles?
choices: Guest Inviter
User Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Directory Writers
questions.answer: Guest Inviter
questions.explanation: Guest Inviter can invite external users and nothing more, so it is the least-privileged role. User Administrator can also invite guests but adds broad user and group management rights.

questions.stem: Contoso must allow B2B invitations only to users from fabrikam.com and wingtiptoys.com. Invitations to any other domain must fail. What should you configure?
choices: Collaboration restrictions that deny invitations to the specified domains
Collaboration restrictions that allow invitations only to the specified domains
Guest invite restrictions that allow only users assigned to specific admin roles to invite
Inbound cross-tenant access settings that block the default organization
questions.answer: Collaboration restrictions that allow invitations only to the specified domains
questions.explanation: An allow list in the collaboration restrictions blocks invitations to every domain that is not listed. A deny list does the opposite, and blocking inbound access by default would not stop invitations to people from non-Entra domains such as consumer email providers.

questions.stem: Partner users who no longer work with Northwind Traders want to remove their own guest accounts without opening a support ticket. Which setting controls whether they can do this?
choices: Guest self-service sign-up
Reset redemption status
External user leave settings
Cross-tenant automatic redemption
questions.answer: External user leave settings
questions.explanation: External user leave settings decide whether external users can remove themselves from your organization. Guest self-service sign-up controls how new external users create accounts, not how they leave.

questions.stem: Litware publishes a supplier portal app. Suppliers should be able to create their own guest accounts when they first open the app, without anyone sending them an invitation. What should you do?
choices: Send a bulk invitation to every supplier contact from a CSV file each month
Create a cross-tenant synchronization configuration
Enable inbound B2B direct connect for all organizations
Enable guest self-service sign-up and associate a user flow with the app
questions.answer: Enable guest self-service sign-up and associate a user flow with the app
questions.explanation: Self-service sign-up user flows let external users register for a specific app on their own. A bulk invitation still requires an admin to know and invite every contact in advance.

questions.stem: A new Microsoft Entra tenant still has its default external collaboration settings. Which statement describes who can invite guest users?
choices: Anyone in the organization, including guests and non-admin members
Only users assigned to specific admin roles
Member users and admin roles, but not guests
No one, until an administrator turns on guest invitations for the tenant
questions.answer: Anyone in the organization, including guests and non-admin members
questions.explanation: The default and most inclusive guest invite setting lets anyone in the organization, guests included, send invitations. Restricting invitations to admin roles is an option administrators must choose.

questions.stem: Adatum's partner team gives you a spreadsheet of 350 external consultants who need guest access next week. You must invite them with the LEAST administrative effort from the admin center. What should you use?
choices: One invitation per consultant from the New user option
A cross-tenant synchronization job to the partner tenant
The bulk invite operation with a completed CSV template
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync with a CSV import connector
questions.answer: The bulk invite operation with a completed CSV template
questions.explanation: Bulk invite takes a CSV of email addresses and redirect URLs and creates all the invitations in one operation. Cross-tenant synchronization is designed for tenants that belong to the same organization and needs configuration in both tenants, so it does not fit a list of outside consultants.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank's onboarding system must create guest invitations automatically whenever a new external auditor is approved. Which method should the developers use?
choices: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
The Microsoft Graph invitations API
A guest self-service sign-up user flow
An access review of all guest users
questions.answer: The Microsoft Graph invitations API
questions.explanation: The invitations API (invitation manager) lets an application invite external users and optionally send the email. Connect Sync only synchronizes objects from on-premises Active Directory.

questions.stem: A contractor at a small firm is invited as a guest. The firm has no Microsoft Entra tenant, the contractor has no Microsoft account, and no federation is configured. Email one-time passcode is enabled. How will the contractor authenticate when redeeming the invitation?
choices: With a Temporary Access Pass issued by your help desk
With Google federation through the default identity provider
With seamless single sign-on from the contractor's laptop
With a one-time passcode sent to the invited email address
questions.answer: With a one-time passcode sent to the invited email address
questions.explanation: When no other identity is available, email one-time passcode sends a code to the invited address for each sign-in. A Temporary Access Pass is an authentication method for your own users, not a redemption method for guests.

questions.stem: An admin invites guests through the API with the invitation email turned off. The guests are told to sign in to reach their app. Which link lets them redeem the invitation?
choices: A direct link to the app or My Apps that includes your tenant context
The common My Apps address with no tenant information
The self-service password reset page for your tenant
The Microsoft Entra Connect Health portal
questions.answer: A direct link to the app or My Apps that includes your tenant context
questions.explanation: Without the email, a guest redeems by opening a tenant-specific link, such as a direct app link or a My Apps URL with your tenant ID. A common endpoint with no tenant context cannot tell which tenant's invitation to redeem.

questions.stem: A non-admin marketing employee at Proseware must invite an agency contact as a guest. The tenant uses default external collaboration settings. What should you do to let the employee send the invitation?
choices: Assign the employee the Guest Inviter role
Assign the employee the User Administrator role
Nothing, because member users can invite guests by default
Change the guest invite setting to admin roles only
questions.answer: Nothing, because member users can invite guests by default
questions.explanation: By default, anyone in the organization can invite guests, so no role is needed. Guest Inviter is required only after invitations have been restricted to admin roles.

questions.stem: A guest from Fabrikam accidentally redeemed your invitation with a personal Microsoft account. She must sign in with her Fabrikam work account and keep her existing group memberships and app assignments. What should you do?
choices: Delete the guest user and send a new invitation
Reset the guest user's redemption status
Change the guest user's userType to Member
Add the guest to a cross-tenant synchronization scope
questions.answer: Reset the guest user's redemption status
questions.explanation: Resetting redemption status keeps the same user object, with its object ID, memberships and assignments, and lets the user redeem again with a different identity. Deleting and reinviting creates a new object and loses that access.

questions.stem: A long-term contractor from a partner company has a B2B guest account. The contractor needs the same directory permissions as employees, but the tenant-wide guest access level must stay unchanged. What should you do?
choices: Set the guest user access level to the same access as members
Assign the contractor the Directory Readers role at the tenant scope
Reset the contractor's redemption status
Change the contractor's userType property from Guest to Member
questions.answer: Change the contractor's userType property from Guest to Member
questions.explanation: The userType property controls whether an external user gets guest or member default permissions, so changing it affects only that account. Changing the guest user access level would affect every guest in the tenant.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes how a B2B collaboration guest user authenticates to your tenant?
choices: Your tenant stores the guest's password hash and validates it at every sign-in
The guest's home tenant copies the user object into your tenant by using Connect Sync
Their home organization or provider authenticates them; your tenant authorizes them
The guest receives a new password from your help desk after the invitation is redeemed
questions.answer: Their home organization or provider authenticates them; your tenant authorizes them
questions.explanation: With B2B collaboration the external identity provider handles authentication, and the guest object in your tenant is used to grant access. Your tenant never stores or validates the guest's home credentials.

questions.stem: Contoso needs a group that automatically contains every external guest account so that a Conditional Access policy can target them. Which dynamic membership rule should you use?
choices: (user.userType -eq "Guest")
(user.accountEnabled -eq false)
(user.department -eq "External")
(user.usageLocation -ne "US")
questions.answer: (user.userType -eq "Guest")
questions.explanation: The userType attribute identifies guest accounts, so a rule on userType equal to Guest captures them. Department or usage location values are set by administrators and do not reliably identify external users.

questions.stem: Wide World Importers has hundreds of guest accounts. Each quarter, the internal sponsor of every guest must confirm whether access is still needed, and denied guests must be removed automatically. The tenant has Microsoft Entra ID Governance licenses. What should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for guests
A recurring access review of guest users with auto-apply of results
A user risk policy in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Guest user access restricted to their own directory objects
questions.answer: A recurring access review of guest users with auto-apply of results
questions.explanation: Access reviews let sponsors or managers attest to continued access on a schedule, and auto-apply removes denied users. Conditional Access controls how guests sign in but never removes stale accounts.

questions.stem: Contoso wants each guest account to record which internal employees are accountable for it, so that those employees can be asked to approve access later. Which user property should you populate?
choices: Manager
Company name
Employee ID
Sponsors
questions.answer: Sponsors
questions.explanation: The sponsors property names the internal users or groups responsible for a guest and can be used by governance features such as access reviews. The manager attribute describes a reporting line, not accountability for an external account.

questions.stem: Contoso and Fabrikam use separate Microsoft Entra tenants. They want users from both companies to work in Microsoft Teams shared channels without creating guest accounts. What must be configured?
choices: B2B collaboration inbound settings in the Contoso tenant only
B2B direct connect inbound and outbound settings in both tenants
A cross-tenant synchronization job from Fabrikam to Contoso
SAML/WS-Fed identity provider federation set up between the two tenants
questions.answer: B2B direct connect inbound and outbound settings in both tenants
questions.explanation: Teams shared channels rely on B2B direct connect, which is blocked by default and works only when each organization enables it for the other. B2B collaboration creates guest objects, which the companies want to avoid.

questions.stem: Contoso's Conditional Access policy requires MFA for all guests. Users from Fabrikam already complete MFA in their own tenant and complain about being prompted twice. What should you configure in Contoso?
choices: Inbound trust settings that accept MFA claims from the Fabrikam tenant
Outbound trust settings that accept MFA claims from Fabrikam
An exclusion for all guests in the Conditional Access policy
Collaboration restrictions that allow invitations only to the Fabrikam domain
questions.answer: Inbound trust settings that accept MFA claims from the Fabrikam tenant
questions.explanation: Inbound trust settings let your Conditional Access policies accept MFA performed in the user's home tenant. Excluding guests from the policy would remove the MFA requirement entirely rather than honoring Fabrikam's MFA.

questions.stem: Contoso wants to stop its users from accessing resources in other organizations' tenants with their Contoso accounts, except for the tenant of its partner Litware. What should you configure?
choices: Block default inbound B2B collaboration and add Litware as an organization with inbound access allowed
Collaboration restrictions that allow invitations only to the Litware domain
Block default outbound B2B collaboration and add Litware with outbound access allowed
Guest invite restrictions set to only users assigned to specific admin roles
questions.answer: Block default outbound B2B collaboration and add Litware with outbound access allowed
questions.explanation: Outbound settings control how your users reach other tenants, and an organizational setting for Litware overrides the blocked default. Inbound settings and collaboration restrictions control external users coming into Contoso.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank worries that employees on corporate devices could sign in to an unknown external tenant with a different account and upload company data. Which feature should you configure to block this?
choices: Outbound B2B collaboration settings
External user leave settings
Inbound B2B direct connect settings
Tenant restrictions v2
questions.answer: Tenant restrictions v2
questions.explanation: Tenant restrictions v2 controls which external tenants and identities can be used from your managed devices or network, including accounts that are not yours. Outbound settings only govern your own users' accounts.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the default cross-tenant access settings in a new Microsoft Entra tenant?
choices: B2B collaboration is allowed, and B2B direct connect is blocked
B2B collaboration is blocked, and B2B direct connect is allowed
B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect are both blocked
B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect are both allowed
questions.answer: B2B collaboration is allowed, and B2B direct connect is blocked
questions.explanation: By default, inbound and outbound B2B collaboration are open while B2B direct connect is blocked until both organizations enable it. That is why Teams shared channels need explicit configuration.

questions.stem: Fabrikam users should be invited to Contoso only to use a single project management app. Other Contoso applications must not be reachable by Fabrikam guests. What should you configure in Contoso?
choices: A default outbound B2B collaboration setting that allows only that application for every external tenant
An external user leave setting scoped to users from the Fabrikam domain
An organizational inbound B2B collaboration setting for Fabrikam that allows only that application
A cross-tenant synchronization scoping filter on the application
questions.answer: An organizational inbound B2B collaboration setting for Fabrikam that allows only that application
questions.explanation: Inbound B2B collaboration settings for a specific organization can limit which applications its users can access. Outbound settings apply to Contoso's own users, not to Fabrikam guests.

questions.stem: Contoso acquired Litware, and both tenants will remain in place. Litware user accounts must be created, updated and removed automatically in the Contoso tenant as Litware staff join, change roles or leave. What should you implement?
choices: A weekly bulk invitation from a CSV export
Cross-tenant synchronization from Litware to Contoso
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync from Litware's tenant
B2B direct connect between the two tenants
questions.answer: Cross-tenant synchronization from Litware to Contoso
questions.explanation: Cross-tenant synchronization automates the lifecycle of B2B users between tenants in the same organization. Bulk invitations create accounts once but never update or remove them.

questions.stem: You must configure the cross-tenant synchronization job in the source tenant. Cross-tenant access settings are already done. Which role should you assign by following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Global Administrator
Hybrid Identity Administrator
User Administrator
Identity Governance Administrator
questions.answer: Hybrid Identity Administrator
questions.explanation: Hybrid Identity Administrator is the least-privileged role documented for configuring cross-tenant synchronization. Global Administrator works but grants far more permissions than needed.

questions.stem: Fabrikam will push users into Contoso with cross-tenant synchronization. What must a Contoso administrator configure in the Contoso tenant for the synchronization to succeed?
choices: Outbound cross-tenant access settings for Fabrikam that allow users to be synchronized out of the tenant
A Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server joined to the Fabrikam forest
A SAML/WS-Fed identity provider for the Fabrikam domain
Inbound cross-tenant access settings for Fabrikam that allow users to sync into the tenant
questions.answer: Inbound cross-tenant access settings for Fabrikam that allow users to sync into the tenant
questions.explanation: The target tenant must allow users from the source tenant to be synchronized in through its inbound settings. Outbound settings in the target tenant control its own users, not incoming synchronization.

questions.stem: Users synchronized into Contoso from the Northwind tenant arrive as external members. Contoso policy requires them to be created with guest default permissions instead. What should you change?
choices: The userType attribute mapping in the synchronization configuration
The guest user access level in the tenant's external collaboration settings
The scoping filter on the synchronization configuration
The redemption status of each synchronized user
questions.answer: The userType attribute mapping in the synchronization configuration
questions.explanation: Cross-tenant synchronization creates users with userType Member by default, and the attribute mapping can set it to Guest. The guest user access level changes permissions for all guests but does not change what type synchronized users become.

questions.stem: Synchronized users from the source tenant see a consent prompt the first time they access the target tenant. You need to suppress this prompt. What should you configure?
choices: Automatic redemption only in the target tenant's inbound settings for the source tenant
Inbound trust settings for MFA and compliant devices
Automatic redemption in the source outbound and the target inbound settings
Admin consent for each application in the target tenant
questions.answer: Automatic redemption in the source outbound and the target inbound settings
questions.explanation: The consent prompt is suppressed only when automatic redemption is enabled on both sides: outbound in the source tenant and inbound in the target tenant. Enabling it on one side alone leaves the prompt in place.

questions.stem: Wingtip Toys uses a third-party SAML 2.0 identity provider and has no Microsoft Entra tenant. Contoso wants Wingtip guests to sign in with their existing Wingtip credentials. What should you configure?
choices: A SAML/WS-Fed identity provider for the Wingtip domain
Google federation with the Wingtip domain
Inbound trust settings for the Wingtip tenant
A Microsoft Entra Connect Sync connector for Wingtip
questions.answer: A SAML/WS-Fed identity provider for the Wingtip domain
questions.explanation: SAML/WS-Fed identity provider federation lets guests from a partner domain authenticate against the partner's own IdP. Inbound trust settings apply to other Microsoft Entra tenants, which Wingtip does not have.

questions.stem: Contoso invites many freelancers who use consumer Gmail addresses. They want to redeem invitations and sign in with their Google accounts. What should you add?
choices: Facebook as an identity provider
A SAML identity provider for gmail.com
An inbound cross-tenant access setting
Google as an identity provider
questions.answer: Google as an identity provider
questions.explanation: The built-in Google identity provider lets guests with Gmail accounts sign in with them. Facebook covers only Facebook accounts, and a SAML/WS-Fed identity provider is meant for partner organizations that run their own IdP.

questions.stem: Fabrikam guests redeemed Contoso invitations months ago by using email one-time passcode. Contoso has now configured SAML/WS-Fed federation for the Fabrikam domain. The existing guests should sign in through Fabrikam's IdP. What should you do?
choices: Delete and reinvite each existing Fabrikam guest
Reset the redemption status of the existing Fabrikam guests
Turn off email one-time passcode for the tenant
Change the existing guests' userType to Member
questions.answer: Reset the redemption status of the existing Fabrikam guests
questions.explanation: Guests who already redeemed keep their original method until their redemption status is reset, after which they redeem again through the new federation and keep their access. Deleting and reinviting loses group memberships and assignments.

questions.stem: Which protocols can you use when you set up identity provider federation for B2B guest users from a partner organization's own IdP?
choices: Kerberos and NTLM
RADIUS and LDAP
SAML 2.0 and WS-Federation
OAuth 1.0 and SAML 1.1
questions.answer: SAML 2.0 and WS-Federation
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra B2B supports partner identity providers that use SAML 2.0 or WS-Fed. Kerberos, NTLM, RADIUS and LDAP are on-premises protocols that are not used for this federation.

questions.stem: Contoso plans to add Facebook as an identity provider for external users. In which scenario can external users sign in with their Facebook accounts?
choices: When they sign up through a self-service sign-up user flow
When they redeem an invitation sent by an admin
When they join a Teams shared channel through B2B direct connect
When they are added by cross-tenant synchronization
questions.answer: When they sign up through a self-service sign-up user flow
questions.explanation: Facebook is available as an identity provider only for self-service sign-up user flows. Invited users redeem with their Entra, Microsoft, Google, federated or one-time passcode identities instead.

questions.stem: You are preparing the CSV template for a bulk guest invitation. Which TWO values are required on each row?
choices: Email address to invite
Redirection URL
Display name
Customized invitation message
Department
Sponsor object ID
questions.explanation: The bulk invite template requires the email address to invite and the redirection URL where the user lands after redeeming. Settings such as a customized invitation message are optional, and department and sponsor are not set through the bulk invite template.

questions.stem: Match each requirement to the cross-tenant access feature that meets it.

pairs.item: Let partner users join Teams shared channels without guest accounts
Honor MFA that partner users already completed in their home tenant
Stop your users from using their accounts in other organizations' tenants
Block unknown external accounts on your managed devices
Suppress the consent prompt for synchronized users

questions.explanation: Shared channels need B2B direct connect; inbound trust accepts partner MFA claims; outbound settings govern your users going out; tenant restrictions control external identities on your devices; automatic redemption removes the consent prompt. Collaboration restrictions limit which domains can be invited, which none of these require.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to set up cross-tenant synchronization from a source tenant to a target tenant.
items: In the target tenant, allow users sync and inbound automatic redemption for the source tenant
In the source tenant, create the synchronization configuration and test the connection to the target
Assign the users or groups that are in scope to the configuration
Test one in-scope user with provision on demand
questions.explanation: The target must accept incoming synchronization before the source tenant's configuration can connect to it (the source also enables outbound automatic redemption). Scoping and an on-demand test come before starting the job so a mistake affects one user rather than everyone.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to let guests from a partner sign in through the partner's own SAML identity provider.
items: Have the partner add Microsoft Entra ID as a relying party and share its IdP metadata
Add a SAML/WS-Fed identity provider for the partner domain in your tenant
Invite partner users, or reset redemption for existing ones
Test sign-in by using a tenant-specific link
questions.explanation: Federation needs the partner's IdP trusting Microsoft Entra ID and its metadata before you can create the identity provider entry. Only then will new or reset guests redeem through it, and a tenant-specific link confirms the flow.

questions.stem: Contoso runs one Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server. If it fails, the company must restore synchronization quickly with a server that already holds the current configuration. What should you deploy?
choices: A second active Connect Sync server that exports to the same tenant
A second Connect Sync server in staging mode
A Connect Health agent for sync on a second server
A pass-through authentication agent on a second server
questions.answer: A second Connect Sync server in staging mode
questions.explanation: A staging mode server imports and synchronizes the same data but does not export, so it can be switched to active if the primary fails. Two active servers exporting to one tenant is not supported.

questions.stem: Litware's forest has dozens of organizational units, but only accounts in the Sales and Engineering OUs should appear in Microsoft Entra ID. What should you configure?
choices: Group-based filtering on a group of all users
A Conditional Access policy that blocks other OUs
Collaboration restrictions in external settings
Domain and OU-based filtering in Connect Sync
questions.answer: Domain and OU-based filtering in Connect Sync
questions.explanation: OU-based filtering limits which containers Connect Sync reads, which is the supported way to scope by location. Group-based filtering is intended for pilots, and Conditional Access controls sign-in, not which objects are synchronized.

questions.stem: An admin removed a large OU from the sync scope by mistake and then fixed it. Later, an intended cleanup deletes 1,200 users from AD DS, and Connect Sync stops exporting with a warning about deletions. You confirmed the deletions are expected. What should you do?
choices: Switch the Connect Sync server into staging mode, then run a full synchronization cycle
Uninstall and reinstall Connect Sync with express settings
Temporarily disable accidental delete prevention, run an export, then turn it back on
Run a full password hash synchronization for all accounts
questions.answer: Temporarily disable accidental delete prevention, run an export, then turn it back on
questions.explanation: Accidental delete prevention blocks exports that exceed the deletion threshold until an admin allows them. Once the deletions are confirmed, you allow the export and re-enable protection; staging mode would stop all exports instead.

questions.stem: Before its first synchronization, Fabrikam wants to find and fix directory problems such as duplicate proxyAddresses and invalid characters in user principal names. Which tool should you use?
choices: IdFix
Synchronization Rules Editor
Connect Health for AD DS
Cloud Sync provisioning logs
questions.answer: IdFix
questions.explanation: IdFix scans on-premises Active Directory for formatting and duplicate errors that would cause synchronization failures and helps fix them. The Synchronization Rules Editor changes attribute flows but does not clean source data.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank needs a custom attribute flow in Connect Sync that survives future upgrades. What is the recommended approach?
choices: Create a new rule with higher precedence in the Synchronization Rules Editor
Edit the matching out-of-box rule directly in the Synchronization Rules Editor
Change the attribute value in the Connect Sync database by using SQL
Add a claim rule on the AD FS relying party trust
questions.answer: Create a new rule with higher precedence in the Synchronization Rules Editor
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends leaving default rules unchanged and adding new rules with a lower precedence number, which wins over the defaults. Edited default rules can be overwritten or cause conflicts when Connect Sync is upgraded.

questions.stem: An administrator changed several user attributes in AD DS and does not want to wait for the next scheduled cycle. Which command starts a synchronization of only the changes?
choices: Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Initial
Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta
Set-ADSyncScheduler -SyncCycleEnabled $true
Restart-Service -Name ADSync
questions.answer: Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta
questions.explanation: A delta cycle processes only the changes since the last run, which is what is needed here. An initial cycle performs a full import and synchronization, which takes much longer and is meant for configuration changes.

questions.stem: You must install and configure Microsoft Entra Connect Sync with password hash synchronization for a new tenant. Which Microsoft Entra role should the installing account hold, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Global Administrator
Security Administrator
User Administrator
Hybrid Identity Administrator
questions.answer: Hybrid Identity Administrator
questions.explanation: Hybrid Identity Administrator, assigned directly to the installing account, can install and configure Connect Sync and features such as password hash synchronization. Global Administrator also works but grants far more access, and Security Administrator and User Administrator cannot complete the setup.

questions.stem: Contoso acquired a company whose AD DS forest has no network connectivity to Contoso's forest. Both sets of users must be synchronized to Contoso's tenant with the least on-premises infrastructure. What should you deploy in the acquired forest?
choices: A second Connect Sync server in staging mode
A two-way forest trust and the existing Connect Sync server
A Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync provisioning agent
A cross-tenant synchronization configuration
questions.answer: A Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync provisioning agent
questions.explanation: Cloud Sync supports disconnected forests because each lightweight agent talks only to the cloud. Connect Sync needs network line of sight to every forest it reads, so it would require new connectivity or a trust.

questions.stem: Fabrikam synchronizes with Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. Synchronization must keep running if the server that hosts the provisioning agent goes offline. What should you do?
choices: Configure a second server in staging mode
Install provisioning agents on additional servers
Move the configuration database to a SQL Server cluster
Install the Connect Health agent for sync
questions.answer: Install provisioning agents on additional servers
questions.explanation: Cloud Sync supports several active provisioning agents for high availability, and the cloud service uses whichever is available. Staging mode is a Connect Sync concept and does not apply to Cloud Sync.

questions.stem: Northwind wants to move from Connect Sync to Cloud Sync. Which requirement would still need configuration outside Cloud Sync?
choices: Pass-through authentication
Password hash synchronization
Password writeback for self-service reset
Synchronization from multiple connected forests
questions.answer: Pass-through authentication
questions.explanation: Cloud Sync supports password hash synchronization, password writeback and multiple forests, but it does not configure pass-through authentication, which is managed separately. That makes PTA the item that falls outside Cloud Sync.

questions.stem: Adatum uses Connect Sync for its main forest and wants to pilot Cloud Sync for a newly added OU in the same forest. What should you do to keep both tools working correctly?
choices: Stop the Connect Sync scheduler until the Cloud Sync pilot has ended
Scope both tools to the same OU for redundancy
Switch the Connect Sync server into staging mode
Scope Cloud Sync to the new OU and exclude it from Connect Sync
questions.answer: Scope Cloud Sync to the new OU and exclude it from Connect Sync
questions.explanation: Connect Sync and Cloud Sync can run side by side as long as each object is in scope of only one of them. Overlapping scopes lead to conflicts, and staging mode would stop Connect Sync from exporting the main forest.

questions.stem: Proseware is choosing between Connect Sync and Cloud Sync. One security group in AD DS has about 120,000 members and must be synchronized intact. Which statement is correct?
choices: Cloud Sync is required, because Connect Sync supports smaller groups
Either tool works, because neither limits group size
Connect Sync is required, because Cloud Sync supports smaller groups
Neither tool works, so the group must be recreated in the cloud
questions.answer: Connect Sync is required, because Cloud Sync supports smaller groups
questions.explanation: Microsoft documents a 250,000-member group limit for Connect Sync and a 50,000-member limit for Cloud Sync, so only Connect Sync fits this group. Cloud Sync is otherwise the lighter option, which makes it the tempting choice.

questions.stem: Contoso uses pass-through authentication. The security team wants Microsoft Entra ID Protection to report leaked credentials for hybrid users. What should you enable?
choices: Password hash synchronization
Seamless single sign-on
AD FS extranet smart lockout
Additional authentication agents
questions.answer: Password hash synchronization
questions.explanation: Leaked credentials detection compares known breached credentials against synchronized password hashes, so password hash synchronization must be enabled even if users sign in with another method. More PTA agents only add sign-in capacity.

questions.stem: What does Microsoft Entra Connect Sync send to Microsoft Entra ID when password hash synchronization is enabled?
choices: The user's password encrypted with the tenant's public key
The unmodified NTLM hash from AD DS
A salted hash derived from the AD DS password hash
A Kerberos ticket issued by a domain controller
questions.answer: A salted hash derived from the AD DS password hash
questions.explanation: Connect Sync applies a salt and a key derivation function to the existing AD DS hash, so neither the password nor the original hash leaves the network. Sending the raw NTLM hash would allow pass-the-hash attacks against the cloud copy.

questions.stem: Fabrikam's domain is federated with AD FS. Management wants a way to keep users signing in to Microsoft 365 if the AD FS farm becomes unavailable. What should you enable in advance?
choices: Seamless single sign-on for all users
Password hash synchronization as a backup
A second AD FS farm in staging mode
Connect Health for AD FS alerts
questions.answer: Password hash synchronization as a backup
questions.explanation: With hashes already synchronized, the domain can be switched to managed authentication during an AD FS outage. Connect Health would only alert on the outage, and seamless SSO does not work with federated domains.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys wants cloud authentication for hybrid users that does not depend on any on-premises servers at sign-in time and needs the least infrastructure. Which method should you choose?
choices: Pass-through authentication
Federation with AD FS
Seamless single sign-on alone
Password hash synchronization
questions.answer: Password hash synchronization
questions.explanation: With password hash synchronization, Microsoft Entra ID validates passwords itself, so sign-in continues even if on-premises servers are down. Pass-through authentication needs on-premises agents and domain controllers available for every sign-in.

questions.stem: Litware uses only password hash synchronization. An admin disables a departing user's account in AD DS. When is the user blocked from signing in to Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: Immediately, because each sign-in checks AD DS
Only after the user's password expires
After the change is synchronized in a sync cycle
Only after the user's cloud password is reset
questions.answer: After the change is synchronized in a sync cycle
questions.explanation: With password hash synchronization, the disabled state reaches the cloud through synchronization, so there is a short delay. Real-time checks against AD DS at each sign-in happen with pass-through authentication, not here.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank requires that on-premises account states, such as disabled accounts and logon hours, apply immediately at cloud sign-in, and that no password hashes are stored in the cloud. Which sign-in method should you implement?
choices: Pass-through authentication
Password hash synchronization
Seamless single sign-on alone
Cloud Sync with password writeback
questions.answer: Pass-through authentication
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication validates each sign-in against AD DS through on-premises agents, so account states and logon hours apply at once. Password hash synchronization stores hash data in the cloud and only picks up changes at the next sync.

questions.stem: Contoso runs pass-through authentication with a single agent on the Connect Sync server. You need to make sign-in resilient if that server fails. What should you do?
choices: Install a second Connect Sync server in staging mode
Install more authentication agents on other servers
Enable seamless single sign-on
Install Connect Health for AD DS
questions.answer: Install more authentication agents on other servers
questions.explanation: PTA agents work active-active, and Microsoft recommends at least three in production so another agent handles requests if one fails. A staging server does not process pass-through sign-ins.

questions.stem: The network team asks which inbound firewall ports must be opened for the pass-through authentication agents. What should you tell them?
choices: TCP 443 inbound from the Microsoft Entra service
TCP 389 inbound from the internet to the agents
TCP 88 inbound from Microsoft Entra ID to each of the agent servers
None, because the agents make outbound connections only
questions.answer: None, because the agents make outbound connections only
questions.explanation: PTA agents establish outbound connections to Microsoft Entra ID and wait for requests over them, so no inbound ports are needed. Opening inbound HTTPS from the internet is a common assumption but is not required.

questions.stem: Fabrikam uses pass-through authentication. Attackers trying passwords from the internet are locking out AD DS accounts. How should you configure Microsoft Entra smart lockout?
choices: Set its lockout threshold higher than the AD DS lockout threshold
Set its threshold equal to the AD DS threshold
Turn it off and rely on the AD DS lockout policy
Set its lockout threshold lower than the AD DS lockout threshold
questions.answer: Set its lockout threshold lower than the AD DS lockout threshold
questions.explanation: When the cloud threshold is lower, smart lockout blocks attackers in Microsoft Entra ID before the attempts reach AD DS and lock the on-premises account. A higher threshold lets AD DS lockouts happen first.

questions.stem: Users on domain-joined Windows devices on the corporate network should reach Microsoft Entra apps without typing their passwords. The company uses password hash synchronization. What should you enable?
choices: Pass-through authentication
Seamless single sign-on
Staged rollout
Microsoft Entra Connect Health
questions.answer: Seamless single sign-on
questions.explanation: Seamless SSO uses Kerberos from domain-joined devices on the corporate network to sign users in silently, and it works with PHS or PTA. Pass-through authentication alone still prompts for a password.

questions.stem: When you enable seamless single sign-on in Connect Sync, which object is created in each on-premises AD DS forest?
choices: A computer account that represents Microsoft Entra ID
A user account used by the provisioning agent
A group managed service account for the sync service
A service connection point for device registration
questions.answer: A computer account that represents Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explanation: Seamless SSO creates a computer account named AZUREADSSOACC in each forest, and its Kerberos decryption key is shared securely with Microsoft Entra ID. A service connection point is used for hybrid join, not seamless SSO.

questions.stem: Your security baseline requires protecting the key that seamless single sign-on uses. Which practice does Microsoft recommend?
choices: Add the computer account to the Domain Admins group
Disable the computer account between sync cycles
Roll over the Kerberos decryption key of its computer account regularly
Store the computer account password in a shared vault for the help desk team
questions.answer: Roll over the Kerberos decryption key of its computer account regularly
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends rolling over the seamless SSO Kerberos decryption key regularly, for example every 30 days. Disabling the account would break seamless SSO, and adding it to Domain Admins would grant unneeded privilege.

questions.stem: After enabling seamless single sign-on, users on domain-joined devices are still prompted for a password in the browser. Kerberos to domain controllers works. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Add the Entra autologon URL to the Intranet zone by Group Policy
Add the Entra autologon URL to the Restricted sites zone by Group Policy
Enable password writeback in the Connect Sync wizard
Install additional pass-through authentication agents
questions.answer: Add the Entra autologon URL to the Intranet zone by Group Policy
questions.explanation: Browsers send Kerberos tickets only to sites in the Intranet zone, so the autologon URL must be placed there, usually by Group Policy. Putting it in Restricted sites would block it, and PTA agents do not affect silent sign-in.

questions.stem: Contoso's domain is federated with AD FS. Before converting the whole domain, the team wants a pilot group to sign in with password hash synchronization while everyone else stays on AD FS. What should you use?
choices: Domain conversion to managed authentication
A second federated domain for the pilot
Microsoft Entra Connect Health
Staged rollout
questions.answer: Staged rollout
questions.explanation: Staged rollout moves selected groups to cloud authentication while the domain remains federated. Converting the domain switches every user at once, which the team wants to avoid.

questions.stem: An admin configures staged rollout with a dynamic membership group of pilot users, but the group cannot be used. What should the admin do?
choices: Use a Microsoft 365 group with dynamic membership
Use a cloud security group with assigned membership
Nest the dynamic group in a security group
Synchronize the group from AD DS with Cloud Sync
questions.answer: Use a cloud security group with assigned membership
questions.explanation: Staged rollout does not support dynamic or nested groups, and Microsoft recommends cloud security groups to avoid sync delays. Nesting the dynamic group fails for the same reason.

questions.stem: Fabrikam plans to retire AD FS. You need to find which relying party applications in AD FS can move to Microsoft Entra ID and which settings would block them. What should you use?
choices: The Connect Sync errors report
The Risky IP report
The AD FS application activity report
The staged rollout sign-in report
questions.answer: The AD FS application activity report
questions.explanation: The AD FS application activity report lists relying party trusts, their usage, and migration readiness with any blocking settings; it needs the Connect Health agent for AD FS on the federation servers to collect the data. The Risky IP report shows failed sign-in sources, not application readiness.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank wants to use staged rollout to move a pilot group from AD FS to password hash synchronization. What must be in place BEFORE you add the group?
choices: The federated domain converted to managed authentication for all users
The AD FS relying party trust removed
Password hash synchronization enabled with hashes synchronized
Seamless SSO disabled in every forest
questions.answer: Password hash synchronization enabled with hashes synchronized
questions.explanation: Users in a PHS staged rollout must already have their hashes in Microsoft Entra ID, or their cloud sign-in fails. Converting the domain or removing the trust are final steps that come after a successful pilot.

questions.stem: Contoso's AD FS farm shows many extranet lockouts. The security team wants a list of IP addresses with the most failed sign-ins against AD FS. What should you use?
choices: The sign-in risk policy in ID Protection
The AD FS application activity report
The Connect Sync errors report
The Risky IP report in Connect Health for AD FS
questions.answer: The Risky IP report in Connect Health for AD FS
questions.explanation: The Risky IP report in Connect Health for AD FS lists sources with high counts of failed or locked-out sign-ins. The application activity report covers relying party usage, not failed sign-in sources.

questions.stem: Fabrikam wants alerts on domain controller health, such as replication failures, in the same portal it uses for Connect Sync monitoring. What should you do?
choices: Install the Connect Health agent for AD DS on each domain controller
Install a provisioning agent on each domain controller
Install a pass-through authentication agent on each domain controller
Run IdFix on each domain controller
questions.answer: Install the Connect Health agent for AD DS on each domain controller
questions.explanation: Connect Health for AD DS uses an agent on each domain controller to report health, replication and performance. A provisioning agent is for Cloud Sync and does not monitor domain controllers.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys has just installed Microsoft Entra Connect Sync by using a Global Administrator account and wants to review synchronization errors, such as duplicate attributes, in Connect Health. What else must be installed on the sync server?
choices: The Connect Health agent for AD FS
Nothing, because Connect Sync installs the Connect Health sync agent
The Connect Health agent for AD DS
A Log Analytics agent connected to a custom workspace on the sync server
questions.answer: Nothing, because Connect Sync installs the Connect Health sync agent
questions.explanation: The Connect Sync installation includes the Connect Health agent for sync, so the sync errors report is available without extra setup. (If the installation is run with a Hybrid Identity Administrator account instead, the agent is installed in a disabled state.) The AD FS and AD DS agents monitor other servers.

questions.stem: Connect Health for AD FS is installed, but the Risky IP report shows no data. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Password hash synchronization is not enabled for the federated users
Seamless single sign-on is not enabled
The sync server is in staging mode
AD FS auditing is not enabled on the federation servers
questions.answer: AD FS auditing is not enabled on the federation servers
questions.explanation: The AD FS agent reads AD FS audit events, so auditing must be turned on for usage and Risky IP data to appear. Password hash synchronization is unrelated to AD FS sign-in data.

questions.stem: The identity team wants email whenever Microsoft Entra Connect Health raises an alert about the sync service. What should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy for the sync account
An Identity Secure Score improvement action
The Connect Health alert notification settings
An access review of the Hybrid Identity Administrator role
questions.answer: The Connect Health alert notification settings
questions.explanation: Connect Health sends alert email to configured recipients, and you can add the team's addresses in its notification settings. Conditional Access and access reviews do not deliver service health alerts.

questions.stem: Match each Microsoft Entra Connect Sync feature to its description.

pairs.match: Imports and synchronizes but does not export changes
Scopes synchronization to members of one pilot group
Immutable link between an AD object and its cloud object
Stops exports when deletions exceed a threshold
Writes cloud password changes back to AD DS

targets_extra: Validates passwords against a domain controller at sign-in
questions.explanation: Staging mode keeps a ready standby; group filtering is for pilots; the source anchor ties objects together for life; delete prevention guards against mass deletions; password writeback supports self-service reset. Validating passwords against a domain controller is pass-through authentication, not a Connect Sync feature.

questions.stem: Contoso uses pass-through authentication. You need to keep users able to sign in if the server hosting the only authentication agent fails. Which TWO actions should you take?
choices: Install additional authentication agents on other servers
Enable password hash synchronization as a backup
Enable seamless single sign-on
Add a Connect Sync server in staging mode
Install Connect Health for AD FS
Enable accidental delete prevention
answers: Install additional authentication agents on other servers
Enable password hash synchronization as a backup
questions.explanation: More agents keep PTA available if one server fails, and synchronized hashes let you switch to password hash synchronization during a wider outage. Seamless SSO still depends on PTA or PHS to complete sign-in, and a staging server does not process PTA requests.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to deploy seamless single sign-on for domain-joined devices.
items: Confirm that password hash synchronization or pass-through authentication is in place
Enable seamless SSO in Connect Sync with domain admin credentials for each forest
Add the autologon URL to the Intranet zone for pilot users by Group Policy
Test sign-in from a domain-joined device on the corporate network
questions.explanation: Seamless SSO adds silent sign-in on top of PHS or PTA, so those come first; enabling it creates the computer account in each forest. Browser zone settings are then deployed to a pilot before testing on the corporate network.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to migrate from AD FS federation to password hash synchronization.
items: Enable password hash synchronization and seamless SSO in Connect Sync
Use staged rollout to move pilot groups and validate sign-in
Convert the federated domain to managed authentication
Confirm that no Microsoft Entra sign-ins still reach AD FS
Remove the relying party trust and decommission AD FS
questions.explanation: Hashes must be in the cloud and silent sign-in ready before any users move, and staged rollout proves the change on a pilot. Only after the domain is converted and verified can AD FS be retired.
